problem: An agent loops, overspends or leaves tools running after cancellation.
principle: Runtime enforces steps, deadlines, cost and state. Reserve before calls, reconcile receipts and retain unknown outcomes.
solutions: History recovers orchestration; Activities perform/retry effects
Long waits and reliable external steps
Service operations, deterministic replay and external idempotency
check: Does a deadline check prove a remote effect was cancelled?
answer: No. It limits new work; committed effects may require query or compensation.

procedures.state: Steps, deadline, spent and reserved tokens/cost.
procedures.failure: Balance checks race; reserve atomically and retain unknown-call liability.
procedures.measure: Step/deadline limits and concurrent reservation bounds.
procedures.case: With funds for one call, two workers cannot both reserve it.

procedures.state: State, checkpoint, pending nodes and approved action hash.
procedures.failure: Interrupt nodes restart; isolate idempotent external effects.
procedures.measure: Crash recovery, repeated resumes and changed proposals.
procedures.case: Approval replay creates nothing; execution uses stable operation_id.

procedures.state: Workflow ID, history, Activity attempts and operation key.
procedures.failure: Workflow replay must be deterministic; Activities may repeat remote writes.
procedures.measure: Restart a worker and verify waits/retries resume without duplicate effects.
procedures.case: Continue after next-day approval without holding an HTTP request open.

scope: The main code checks local step/deadline budgets. Framework and outbox references state their recovery limits; deadline checks do not guarantee cancellation of an external call already issued.
